evidence.description: Entity positions, directions and footprints read losslessly from the selected blueprint leaf. Geometry only: adjacency is not a claim about engine behaviour.

belt.straight.lane_capacity [documented-only]: A straight fast-transport-belt carries at most 30 items/s across both lanes and 15 items/s per lane, matching prototype speed 0.0625 tiles/tick x 480. transport-belt is 15/s (7.5 per lane) and express is 45/s (22.5 per lane). Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

belt.side_load.lane_assignment [pending]: A perpendicular side-load is expected to feed a specific lane of the target belt determined by the load's side, and the target's own upstream flow competes for that lane. Which lane, and the resulting split, is not established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

belt.transfer.belt_to_belt [pending]: An end-to-end handover between two belts of the same direction preserves lane identity and is limited by the slower of the two belts. Neither the lane preservation nor the tier-boundary limit is established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

belt.turn.lane_behavior [pending]: A turn is expected not to reduce a saturated lane's throughput, but the inner and outer lanes traverse different path lengths, so per-lane timing differs. The magnitude, and whether any lane loses throughput, is not established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

circuit.control_state [pending]: A circuit-disabled entity does not move items. An entity whose condition state is unknown must remain an explicit condition: relaxed open for an upper bound, or assigned explicitly, never silently enabled or deleted. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

inserter.endpoints.pickup_drop_tiles [documented-only]: Pickup and drop tiles follow the prototype's pickup_position [0, -1] and insert_position [0, 1.2] rotated by the entity direction, so a north-facing inserter takes from the tile one south and drops one north. Documented wiki behaviour adds that an inserter dropping onto a belt places items on the far lane. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

inserter.rate.cycle_and_stack [documented-only]: Throughput is cycles per second times hand size. The wiki gives roughly 0.86 cycles/s for the inserter and 2.5 cycles/s for the fast and bulk inserters at normal quality, and hand size grows with inserter capacity research, which the blueprint does not record. The prototype exposes only extension_speed, rotation_speed and the bulk flag, so no items/s follows from it. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

machine.activity.assembling_machine_2 [documented-only]: An AM2 crafts at crafting_speed 0.75 divided by the recipe's energy_required, with no modules and no beacons. The prototype also advertises 2 module slots and 150kW, which the first profile does not use. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

machine.activity.electric_furnace [documented-only]: An electric furnace crafts smelting recipes at crafting_speed 2.0 divided by energy_required, with source and result inventory size 1. A furnace has no recipe field in a blueprint, so its recipe follows from what is inserted and is a candidate set until assigned. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

splitter.lane_split [pending]: A splitter occupies a 2x1 tile footprint with two input tiles and two output tiles, each carrying two lanes, and its total throughput is bounded by the belt tier. Which physical resource the four paths share, and how an unbalanced input is distributed, is not established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

splitter.priority_and_filter [pending]: Priorities and filters restrict how a splitter distributes items. For an optimistic upper bound they must be relaxed explicitly, and the relaxation recorded, rather than modelled as a hard split. The actual behaviour is not established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

underground.pairing.conflict [pending]: An intervening same-tier underground entrance is expected to capture the pairing, splitting the original tunnel; a different tier is expected to pass through. Neither is established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

underground.lane_mapping [pending]: A tunnel is expected to preserve left and right lane identity end to end. Not established here. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

underground.pairing.range [pending]: The prototype's raw max_distance is 5 (underground-belt), 7 (fast) and 9 (express). Whether that number counts the tiles between the pair or the centre-to-centre separation determines the reach by exactly one tile, and the prototype documentation does not say which. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation

unsupported.entity_visibility [documented-only]: An entity outside the first entity set stays visible in the graph as unsupported topology with a subsystem hint, and never becomes a supported activity or an implicit transport link. In the pilot this is the 3 ee-super-substation entities, classified as subsystem 'power', support 'unsupported', origin 'unknown'. Blocking gate: legacy evidence targets base-2.0.76-normal-v1; obtain a compatible base-2.0.77-normal-v1 observation
